newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE PESO LIKELY TO STAY UNDER PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE PESO LIKELY TO STAY UNDER PRESSURE.

text.p: The Philippine peso is expected to remain under pressure from the slowdown of dollar inflows brought on by the turmoil in Asian currency markets, traders said on Thursday.
However, the central bank cut in its overnight borrowing rate by four percentage points to 14 percent on Thursday, is unlikely to have much impact, they added.
"The bigger factor is the lack of inflows because of the pressure on other regional currencies," a trader said.
A trader said the peso could trade in a lower range of 28.80/29.30 to dollar today compared with the previous 28.70/29.10. The peso closed at 29.05 on Wednesday.
"Though it's less expensive to hold on to dollars, it's more of a question of meeting dollar requirements," another said.
"And the rate cut won't give that much encouragement to hold dollars because of the limits imposed by the central bank," he added.
In late July, the central bank cut the limit on banks' long dollar positions to five percent from 10 percent of capital.
